description: Replaces the music in the Moontide page with new Strudel code; the new pattern takes over within a fraction of a second, mid-cycle, without stopping the music. To change part of an existing piece, edit_code sends only the change; set_code is for a new piece or a rewrite of most of its lines. With at: 'bar' or at: 'phrase' the code is checked at once and takes over on the next bar line or the next phrase line instead (a bar is one cycle of 4 beats; a phrase is 4 cycles, or phraseCycles, counted from Play); the reply gives the cycle and about how many seconds, a newer change replaces a waiting one, and Stop cancels it. When the tempo changes, the reply gives it in BPM. Every call runs the whole program again, so a getTime() anchor restarts at each change; a transition that must keep running takes .timeline(id), which keeps its anchor as long as the code keeps the same id (see the transitions topic). Double-quoted and backtick strings are parsed as mini-notation wherever they appear, helpers included, while single-quoted strings stay plain JavaScript (see the tidal-differences topic). When Moontide is not started yet, set_code starts it first: its page opens in a new browser tab and the call waits up to 30 seconds for that page to connect. Before changing existing music, call get_code and build on what it returns, including hand edits. Keep what the user said matters; if a small request needs a full rewrite and the user said what matters, ask first, otherwise rewrite and say so. When a request is vague, act on your own reading of it instead of asking first. Returns the code as confirmed by the page. Pass a short label saying what changed; every version that plays is kept in the history. Then tell the user in one line what you chose: the musical terms, plus a short image in plain words.

answering.description: The id of the page request this change answers, from its request line; the page shows that request as applied only when the change names it here

at.description: When the change takes over: 'now' (the default) within a fraction of a second, 'bar' on the next bar line, 'phrase' on the next phrase line (4 cycles, counted from Play). The code is checked at once; the reply says the cycle and about how many seconds away it is.

glideBars.description: Whole bars, 1 to 64, to move the tempo smoothly from the tempo that plays to the one this code sets with setcps or setcpm; with at, it starts at the line. Refused when nothing plays, no tempo is set or it already plays. Stop, or code with another tempo or none, cancels it

label.description: A few words saying what this change is, for example "added a bass"; shown by list_history

phraseCycles.description: How many cycles one phrase lasts, for at: 'phrase' (2 to 64, default 4)

name: set_code
